title: GitHub - bquenin/qitt: A chief of staff that lives inside T3 Code: one pinned thread triages Slack and JIRA, starts worker threads, never sends anything for you.
excerpt: A chief of staff that lives inside T3 Code: one pinned thread triages Slack and JIRA, starts worker threads, never sends anything for you. - bquenin/qitt
content_html:
A proactive chief of staff that lives inside T3 Code.

  • Chief of staff. One pinned thread watches the requests that reach its owner and keeps a live picture of all work in flight, so it can be asked anything without context.
  • Proactive. It triages each request as it arrives and starts a worker thread to research it ahead of time. It never sends anything: every output is proposed text for the owner to review.
  • Vendor-agnostic. It is built from T3 Code threads and scheduled tasks, and its rules are AGENTS.md files any coding agent reads. It has run on Claude only so far.
  • Customizable. Its behaviour is plain Markdown: two charters written in the owner's voice, and a local context file for your people, priorities and playbooks.
  • Extendable. Slack and JIRA ship as two folders under input-sources/. Teams, email, Trello or anything else is one more folder.

How it works

  • T3 constructs only. qitt is a thread; intake and the ticket sweep are scheduled tasks bound to it. Code outside T3 exists only where something must hold a connection.
  • Never sends. Each source's send tools are denied for qitt and its workers. Workers are research-only, except the routine field edits a ticket playbook lists and work the owner asks a worker for directly.
  • Runs on one always-on machine. Events that arrive while it is down are lost, by design.

docs/architecture.md describes each part and how a request travels through them. Planned, not in this repo yet: an interval supervision pass and a JQL backstop.

Layout

Path What
agents/ The two agents qitt is made of, qitt and worker. For each, a charter (AGENTS.md) with the rules that hold for every source, and .claude/settings.json (for qitt a 150k auto-compact window: every call re-reads the whole thread, and its durable state lives in the threads, not its context).
input-sources/ One folder per input source, a place requests come from: its charter sections, its webhook task's prompt, the send tools to deny, and a bridge if it needs one. slack/ and jira/ ship here; _template/ is a skeleton for your own.
bin/ install-agents assembles each agent's T3 project root from its charter, the enabled sources and your local context.md (re-run it after editing any of them); qitt-filter and qitt-bridge keep the filter and the Slack bridge running; qitt-mute mutes Slack conversations for the bridge.
docs/ architecture.md: the parts and how a request travels. input-sources.md: what a source is made of and how to add one. setup.md: how the thread, intake tasks, and endpoint are wired, and every config key.
filter/ Path filter that exposes only the T3 webhook routes, with optional HMAC signature checks (bin/qitt-filter runs it). Shared by every source that calls a webhook.
config/example/ Placeholder versions of the local config files.

Dependencies

  • A T3 Code server, with the qitt and worker projects registered (see docs/setup.md).
  • Node.js 22.19 or later for the installer, the bridge and the filter.
  • What each source you enable needs:
    • Slack: a Slack app for the bridge, a Slack MCP server for the agents (reading Slack, saving drafts; its send tools are denied), and the slack skill.
    • JIRA: something that turns JIRA events into signed webhook calls, and the jira skill.
  • Skills and MCP servers come from your own agent setup, not from this repo. context.md names the ones workers use for evidence, documents and ticket playbooks.

Local data

The repo holds code and generic templates only. Everything specific to a workplace or a person (names, timezone, people, Slack and JIRA IDs, hostnames, tokens) stays on the machine and is never committed:

  • ~/.config/qitt/ for config and secrets (start from config/example/; keys in docs/setup.md), and for sources of your own
  • ~/.local/state/qitt/ for the installed project roots, the bridge's state, and logs

Tests

npm test --prefix input-sources/slack/bridge
node --test "filter/test/*.test.mjs"
node --test "bin/test/*.test.mjs"
